Cq.bar_b_note: B's dark gold-veined serpent approaches the Fulgocobra board, but A's flat cartoon yellow banding and fully airborne faint frames are not shipping-game finish.

Eu.bar_b_note: B's furred wolf with crisp white-violet arcs sits at Palworld creature finish; the rubbery, lifted faint poses are what still hold it back.

Fl.bar_b_note: The standing ram reads well, but the wool is an unlit white blob and B's faint frames collapse into a smeared, flattened mesh.

Rt.bar_b_note: The white-haired elder in moss-green vest and earth tones has clean, appealing stylised-character finish that fits the key-art settlement.

Nd.bar_b_note: A murky brown floor with no purple storm sky, flat magenta ring and slab telegraphs, a near-invisible player creature and a HUD that covers much of each frame (plus foliage filling B's frames) sink it.

top_changes.change: Stormwood fight (Nd): replace the flat magenta telegraph rings and slabs with white-violet lightning and ground-crack effects that have a real impact, keep the camera out of trunks and foliage, show the purple storm sky, rim-light both fighters, and shrink or fade the HUD side panels during combat

Ground every faint pose: snap the fainted body to the stage so it meets its shadow (Cq A faint mid/end, Eu A and B faint mid/end), and drop Cq side A's yellow-band material for B's dark gold-veined serpent look

Rebuild the faint animations and skin weights that break the read: Stormcapra side B faint mid/end, where the mesh flattens and smears, and Fulgocobra side A, where the faint becomes an upright S-curve in mid-air
